chunks: Al-Muzaffar ibn Ja'far ibn Al-Muzaffar Al-Alawi (may Allah have mercy on him) told us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Mas'ud told us, from his father, from Hamdawayh, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid told us, from Abu Jameela, from Amr ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him about tafath. He said: It is trimming the head.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of tafath in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a concise definition of *tafath* as the grooming or trimming of the head's hair, linking physical cleanliness to ritual purity. This clarification is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between minor grooming acts and major ablution requirements, emphasizing the Sunnah of maintaining personal hygiene as an act of worship.

en.basel-kadem: 6.	We were told by Mufaddar bin Ja’far bin Mudaffar al-Alawi, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ja’far bin Muhammed bin Mas’ud, from his father, from Hamdawayh, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abdul-Hameed, from Abu Jameela, from Amru bin Handhala, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
I asked him about tafath. He said: It is to trim the head.
